The identity matrix is the tuple (1, 0, 0, 1). The matrix J is the tuple (0, -1, 1, 0). Its square is the tuple (-1, 0, 0, -1). Its cube is the tuple (0, 1, -1, 0). The product of J with J equals the square, the product of the square with J equals the cube, and the product of the cube with J equals the identity. J, its square and its cube differ from the identity. The products at 1, 2, 3 and 4 equal J, the square, the cube and the identity. The remainders of 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 on division by 4 are 0, 1, 2, 3 and 0. The integer 0 * 0 - 1 * 1 equals -1, and (-1) * (-1) equals 1.

decisions.statement: A degree-1 window is (C0,C1,C2,d0,d1) of finite-dimensional spaces with a norm J; Q1 = C1/im d0; kappa1([h]) = d1 h is defined exactly when d1 d0 = 0 (the window hypothesis; otherwise no kappa1 exists on Q1), H1 = ker kappa1, Phi1 = quotient defect Phi_J, Gamma2 = L1 norm of d1 h, R_cl = Gamma2/Phi1 only when Phi1 > 0; the diagnostic classes ExactClass (Phi1 = 0), ClosedResidual (Phi1 > 0, Gamma2 = 0), ActiveClosureFailure (Phi1 > 0, Gamma2 > 0) partition the (Phi1, Gamma2) pairs. [Kernel-checked over a field for the algebra and for the abstract defect; for weighted-L1 cost on graph windows with positive weights the cost is proved to be the IsPhi defect of a definite J, so Phi1 = 0 iff the class is zero; Phi1 values on 17 integer windows are certified by verified primal/dual pairs; norms other than weighted L1 and attainment for general windows are not covered.]
decisions.bottleneck: The window is declared, not derived from <> or Real_0 (PG-GAP-GENESIS-TO-WINDOW). Existence of the attained minimum for every weighted-L1 window (strong duality) is not a Lean theorem; per-window attainment rests on verified primal/dual witnesses.
decisions.reason: kappa1 on Q1 exists exactly when d1 d0 = 0; for weighted-L1 graph windows with positive weights the cost is the defect of a definite norm and Phi1 values are certified by verified primal/dual pairs; attainment for general windows and other norms are not covered.

decisions.statement: For weighted-L1 windows with attained minima: if the sub-window's d0 is the restriction of the big d0, its cochain is the restriction and its weights are at most the restrictions, then Phi1(sub) <= Phi1(big), so growth with an extending cochain and weights not lowered never lowers Phi1 (a decrease needs deleting cells, lowered weights, a changed d0 or changed cochain values); attaching a 2-cell whose row satisfies d1 d0 = 0 leaves (D0, w, h) and hence Phi1 unchanged (definitional) and adds |row . h| to Gamma2 = ||d1 h||_1, so Gamma2 cannot decrease. Monotonicity fails when weights are raised, when d0 is not the restriction, or for a norm not monotone under coordinate deletion (norm arithmetic only). Equal-weight subdivision, filtration limit pages, complex coefficients and the existence of minimisers are not covered.
decisions.bottleneck: The source Lean theorems (wdp_growth_subcomplex_monotone, wdp_two_simplex_attachment_preserves_phi1) are a List Nat sum bound and an rfl; the real statement is proved here only under hcompat, restricted cochain, weights not raised and attained minima; equal-weight subdivision and existence of minimisers are unported.
decisions.reason: Restriction monotonicity of Phi1 is kernel-checked for weighted-L1 windows with restricted d0, cochain and non-raised weights and attained minima; the source Lean theorems are a List Nat sum bound and an rfl; equal-weight subdivision and minimiser existence are unported.

decisions.statement: On an unstructured set with at least two elements no point is fixed by every permutation (the bare-set form of: no Sym(X)-equivariant distinguished-point selection exists). In the pointwise-stabiliser model, in which a declared input set is fixed pointwise, the inclusion-minimal declarations that make some point invariant are exactly the singletons (price one declared point; price zero on a one-point carrier; no selection on the empty carrier). The ledger definition D01 of the asymmetry-price frontier relative to an implementation class and dependency preorder is not formalised. The result says selection is not free on a bare set; it does not say retention or observers cannot exist.

decisions.statement: For a window over a field with d1 d0 = 0, kappa1 is well defined on Q1 and 0 -> H1 -> Q1 -> im d1 -> 0 is exact with dim Q1 = dim H1 + dim im d1; when dim H1 > 0 and dim im d1 > 0 no section is invariant under the automorphisms 1 + incl f pi of the extension (which act freely on the sections and are not automorphisms of the window), and when either vanishes the section is unique and invariant; every pair (Phi1, Gamma2) lies in exactly one diagnostic class; for a definite J, Phi1 = 0 iff the class of h is zero (false for a seminorm); and for weighted L1 over Q with an attained minimum, ||d1 h||_1 <= c Phi1 whenever c is at least the largest column-sum-to-weight ratio (equivalent to the operator bound). Naturality of the splitting for automorphisms of the window, other norms, complex coefficients and Phi1 >= 0 are not covered.
decisions.bottleneck: 'No canonical splitting' is proved only for the unipotent automorphisms of the extension (a torsor statement) and is false for dim H1 = 0 or d1 = 0; Gamma2 is the representative norm (equal to the source value at the minimal residual when d1 d0 = 0); the norm hypothesis and an attained minimiser are assumed; naturality for window automorphisms is the node's next test.
decisions.reason: Exactness and unique diagnostic class are kernel-checked over a field; no canonical splitting holds only for dim H1 > 0 and dim im d1 > 0 against the unipotent automorphisms of the extension; Phi1 = 0 iff zero class needs a definite norm; the Gamma2 bound needs the operator-norm hypothesis.
